verses.english: Linked Discourses 7.18
2. Lay Followers
Collecting Firewood

verses.pali: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā kosalesu viharati aññatarasmiṁ vanasaṇḍe.
verses.english: At one time the Buddha was staying in the land of the Kosalans in a certain forest grove.

verses.pali: Tena kho pana samayena aññatarassa bhāradvājagottassa brāhmaṇassa sambahulā antevāsikā kaṭṭhahārakā māṇavakā yena vanasaṇḍo tenupasaṅkamiṁsu; upasaṅkamitvā addasaṁsu bhagavantaṁ tasmiṁ vanasaṇḍe nisinnaṁ pallaṅkaṁ ābhujitvā ujuṁ kāyaṁ paṇidhāya parimukhaṁ satiṁ upaṭṭhapetvā. Disvāna yena bhāradvājagotto brāhmaṇo tenupasaṅkamiṁsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhāradvājagottaṁ brāhmaṇaṁ etadavocuṁ:
verses.english: Then several students, pupils of one of the Bhāradvāja brahmins, approached a forest grove while collecting firewood. They saw the Buddha sitting down cross-legged at the root of a certain sal tree, his body set straight, and mindfulness brought to the present. Seeing this, they went up to Bhāradvāja and said to him,
“Please sir, you should know this.

verses.pali: Asukasmiṁ vanasaṇḍe samaṇo nisinno pallaṅkaṁ ābhujitvā ujuṁ kāyaṁ paṇidhāya parimukhaṁ satiṁ upaṭṭhapetvā”.
verses.english: In such and such a forest grove the ascetic Gotama is sitting down cross-legged, his body set straight, and mindfulness brought to the present.”

verses.pali: Atha kho bhāradvājagotto brāhmaṇo tehi māṇavakehi saddhiṁ yena so vanasaṇḍo tenupasaṅkami.
verses.english: Then Bhāradvāja together with those young students went to that forest grove

verses.pali: Addasā kho bhagavantaṁ tasmiṁ vanasaṇḍe nisinnaṁ pallaṅkaṁ ābhujitvā ujuṁ kāyaṁ paṇidhāya parimukhaṁ satiṁ upaṭṭhapetvā.
verses.english: where he saw the Buddha sitting down cross-legged, his body set straight, and mindfulness brought to the present.

verses.pali: Disvāna yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi:
verses.english: He went up to the Buddha and addressed him in verse:
“Deep in the jungle so full of terrors,
you’ve plunged into the empty, desolate wilderness.
Still, steady, and graceful:
how beautifully you meditate, mendicant!

verses.pali: Na yattha gītaṁ napi yattha vāditaṁ,
verses.english: Where there is no song or music,
a lonely sage resorts to the wilderness.
This strikes me as an amazing thing,
that you dwell so joyfully alone in the jungle.
I suppose you wish to be reborn in the company
of the supreme world-sovereign of the Third Heaven.
Is that why you resort to the desolate wilderness,
to practice fervor for attaining divinity?”
“Any wishes and hopes that are always attached
to the many and various realms—
the yearnings sprung from the root of unknowing—
I’ve eliminated them all down to the root.
So I’m wishless, unattached, uninvolved;
amongst all things, my vision is clear.
I’ve attained the state of grace, <j>the supreme awakening;
I meditate alone, brahmin, and self-assured.”

verses.pali: Evaṁ vutte, bhāradvājagotto brāhmaṇo bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
verses.english: When he had spoken, Bhāradvāja said to the Buddha,
“Excellent, worthy Gotama! Excellent! …
From this day forth, may the worthy Gotama remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge for life.”
